name: Luma
subtitle: the close moon
story: Once a year Luma's moon comes in so close that it hums, a low note you feel in your teeth. Children climb the hill with letters and press them against it as it drifts past. Most are never seen again. Every few years one comes back the following autumn, answered, in handwriting no one recognises. The longest reply so far ran to eleven pages and was mostly questions about dogs.
hook: A planet for people who still write letters.
cover: Kids post letters to the moon.
beats: Once a year the moon comes close enough to touch, so children press letters against it.
Most never come back. Every few years one does, answered, in handwriting no one recognises.
odd_line: Return address: the moon. Postage: none required.
rule: Letters to the moon must be polite. It has answered rude ones.
question: What would you write on yours?
extra: This year's letters go up next week. I'm told to bring a pen.

episode.opener: The moon has questions about dogs.

beats.text:
Each autumn it passes
close enough to touch.

Children press letters to it.
Most never come back.

Every few years, one does.
Answered, in handwriting nobody recognises.

I read the longest one.
Eleven pages. Mostly dogs.
A whole page on sticks.

Frank has written to the moon
every autumn of his life.
Not one reply.

Still, he writes.
Mostly about his dogs.

This autumn, one came back.
'Dear Biscuit,
how is Frank?'

episode.end: Allow one orbit for a reply.
episode.caption:
Luma's moon comes round every October, low enough to clip the hilltops. You hear it a day before you see it: a hum in your back teeth. Every dog on the planet lies down.

A letter pressed to the moon sticks for the whole orbit. Be polite: it has answered rude ones. The eleven-page reply ended with a drawing of a dog, done from description. It was mostly ears. So is Biscuit, Frank's eighth dog and the first to get post.

It has been late once, in 1987. It won't say where it went.

Our own moon drifts 3.8 cm further away every year. Luma's keeps coming back.

I went up this year and wrote about a cat called Everything. Nothing yet.

What would you tell the moon about your dog?

short.title:
The moon here
writes back.
short.sub:
Each autumn,
it's close enough to touch.

beats.text:
Frank writes to it every year,
mostly about his dog, Biscuit.

No reply. Then the moon wrote:
'Dear Biscuit, how is Frank?'
